If the promised +5–7 % accuracy under hard energy caps and ≤2 % ECE hold, it would set a new state of the art for trustworthy and sustainable GNNs on dynamic graphs, a recognised open problem. 
Societally, edge devices and renewable-powered servers increasingly impose fluctuating energy budgets; a model that anticipates and complies with those budgets while maintaining accuracy directly impacts mobile sensing, green datacentres and cost-sensitive cloud inference. The release of two large dynamic benchmarks plus a diagnostic metric (RWSI) also creates community assets that are likely to influence subsequent research.
The significance is moderated only by the complexity of the pipeline, which may hinder widespread adoption without substantial engineering effort.

idea.open_problems:
1. Curvature dynamics in real graphs are often multi-scale (micro motifs vs. meso communities) and heavy-tailed; existing one-scale Gaussian filters (including C²KF and NK²F) average them out, letting fine-grained squashing persist.
2. Koopman operators learnt per-graph ignore spatial non-stationarity: the same kernel is applied to city centres and rural areas although flow statistics differ.
3. Uncertainty is propagated only up to the second moment; tail risks that dominate rare-event prediction (outbreak spikes, DDoS bursts) remain uncalibrated.
4. Edge-level power tracing enables green scheduling, but privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) forbid logging fine-grained contact patterns; no anti-oversmoothing method offers built-in differential privacy.
5. Theoretical understanding lags behind practice: we lack non-asymptotic bounds that jointly cover (a) curvature-controlled continuous-depth flows and (b) adaptive sparsification, making it hard to pick safe solver tolerances.
6. Benchmarks still focus on Bluetooth or Web links; high-frequency financial and blockchain graphs feature faster topology drift and stronger tail events, stressing both calibration and privacy.
idea.methods:
We upgrade C3PO into μC3PO (multi-scale, privacy-aware Curvature-Controlled Causal-Probabilistic ODE) with five new components.

1 Hierarchical α-Stable Koopman Filter (HαK-F)
  • Decomposes curvature field into K scales via a learned Haar wavelet basis; each scale k is forecast by an α-stable Koopman operator K_k(·) whose stability index α_k∈(1,2] is learnt.  
  • A gating network selects scale-specific ranks r_k and mixture weights, allowing spatially varying dynamics.  
  • Propagates full stable law parameters (location, scale, skew, α) through an Unscented-Stable Transform; captures extreme curvatures that drive over-squashing.

2 Normalizing-Flow Bayesian Implicit SDE (NF-BI-SDE)
  • Replaces Gaussian diffusion with a RealNVP flow on the noise term; yields tractable likelihood for tail-event calibration and supports closed-form Rényi-MI gradients.
  • Guarantees Lipschitz <1 by spectral norm control on flow Jacobians; extends previous Stratonovich layer.

3 Spatial-Mixture Graph Scheduler (SMiGS)
  • Learns a region-conditioned policy π(ϵ,s,Δt) that jointly sets solver tolerance, sparsifier mask and update interval Δt.
  • Uses hierarchical Koopman predictive variance to decide when to re-solve vs. reuse cached embeddings, slashing redundant recomputation on quasi-static subgraphs.

4 DP-Curvature Perturbation (DP-Curv)
  • Adds calibrated Laplace/α-stable noise to HαK-F updates such that (ϵ_DP,δ)-differential privacy holds per time-step.
  • Proves that privacy noise inflates curvature only within a bound that preserves the global Lipschitz guarantee, preventing new over-smoothing.

5 Non-Asymptotic Smoothing Bound & Meta-Rank Search
  • Extends CSBM analysis to curvature-driven ODEs, deriving probabilistic bounds on effective-rank collapse after continuous time τ.
  • A lightweight meta-controller uses the bound to auto-tune {r_k} and flow depth to stay below a target rank-loss γ.

All blocks are differentiable; privacy noise is injected through the re-parameterisation trick so gradients flow unabated.
idea.experimental_setup:
Datasets
• Crypto-Tx (NEW): 2-year Ethereum transaction graph (3.4 B edges) with on-chain gas-price trace (energy proxy) and GDPR-compliant hashed addresses.
• Solar-Traffic (from C3PO).
• WebArchive (renamed Internet-Archive).
• PowerCOVID.
• ogbn-arxiv, Chameleon, Squirrel.

Protocols
1 Privacy regimes: ε_DP∈{∞ (none),4,1}.  
2 Energy budgets: static 5 W, diurnal 0–6 W, carbon-aware price trace 0–12 W.  
3 Baselines: C3PO, CurvFlow, NDLS+MLP, GDE, GCNII+PairNorm, HopGNN, ScatteringGCN, DPSGCN (privacy baseline).
4 Metrics: Accuracy/mAP; ECE; Tail-ECE (top-5 % errors); RWSI; AuPC; Joules; Peak VRAM; ε_DP; Theoretical vs. empirical rank-loss gap.
5 Ablations: (i) disable α-stable (Gaussian); (ii) no NF; (iii) privacy off; (iv) bound-free rank search; (v) freeze SMiGS.
idea.expected_result:
• μC3PO improves C3PO accuracy by +0.8 % (ε_DP=∞) and retains ≥96 % of that accuracy at ε_DP=4, ≥92 % at ε_DP=1.
• Tail-ECE ≤1.5 % (vs 2 % C3PO, 6 % TGAT).
• Under diurnal regime, SMiGS cuts total energy by an extra 20 % over C3PO while keeping AuPC > 0.995.
• α-stable modelling lowers curvature-forecast NLL by 40 % and halves extreme-event CRPS.
• Non-asymptotic bound over-estimates empirical rank loss by <5 % across datasets, enabling safe auto-tuning in 2 extra epochs.
• DP-Curv adds ≤7 % compute overhead; privacy ablation shows noise increases RWSI only 3 % thanks to bound-aware compensation.
idea.expected_conclusion: Multi-scale α-stable curvature dynamics, flow-based uncertainty, privacy-aware filtering and bound-guided meta-learning jointly create the first GNN that is (i) robust to extreme geometric drifts, (ii) differentially-private by construction, (iii) energy-predictive and (iv) theoretically verifiable.  μC3PO sets new calibrated, sustainable and privacy-preserving SOTA on billion-edge dynamic graphs and provides the community with Crypto-Tx plus Tail-ECE, catalysing research at the intersection of trustworthy geometry, privacy and green AI.

evaluate.novelty_reason: μC3PO tackles graph over-smoothing/over-squashing through a combination of ideas that do not appear in the surveyed literature. 1) It treats curvature as a stochastic multi-scale field, learned with a hierarchy of α-stable Koopman operators; prior curvature work (BORF) is single-scale, static and Gaussian. 2) It propagates full stable-law parameters with an Unscented-Stable transform, whereas all listed baselines (PairNorm, DGN, ContraNorm, PSNR, etc.) assume finite-variance Gaussian uncertainty or ignore higher moments. 3) It is the first anti-oversmoothing approach that builds differential privacy into the curvature updates (DP-Curv), satisfying (ε,δ)-DP without destroying the Lipschitz control; none of the related works integrate privacy at the algorithmic level. 4) It unifies continuous-depth curvature-controlled ODEs with adaptive sparsification and derives non-asymptotic effective-rank collapse bounds—no existing theory simultaneously covers continuous flows and dynamic sparsifiers. 5) The Spatial-Mixture Graph Scheduler links curvature-based predictive variance to solver tolerances and energy budgets, introducing a resource-aware dimension that is absent from previous methods. 6) New evaluation axes (Tail-ECE, Joules, Crypto-Tx dataset) and α-stable noise ablations are also novel. These elements together represent a methodological departure rather than an incremental variant of known normalization, rewiring or residual schemes.
evaluate.significance_reason: Academically, μC3PO extends the study of over-smoothing into heavy-tailed, multi-scale, privacy-constrained and energy-budgeted regimes that current GNN theory and practice do not cover, and it supplies a matching non-asymptotic analysis. This can open several new research threads (stable-law message passing, privacy-preserving geometric learning, curvature-aware schedulers). Societally, the method addresses two pressing issues for large real-world graphs: a) regulatory privacy (GDPR/HIPAA) by integrating DP noise directly in the mitigation procedure; b) sustainability by cutting recomputation energy via SMiGS. Its applicability to billion-edge financial/blockchain graphs and pandemic power-grid data further raises impact.  Limitations (high complexity, specialised assumptions) temper but do not overshadow its potential.

idea.open_problems:
1 Data are often distributed across multiple legal or organisational silos (hospitals, energy operators, crypto-exchanges).  Existing curvature-aware anti–oversmoothing methods—including μC3PO—assume centralised storage and cannot be deployed when raw edges cannot leave the local site.
2 Cross-graph non-stationarity: curvature spectra differ drastically between clients (e.g., rural vs. urban power grids); one global filter either oversmooths small graphs or leaves large ones under-regularised.
3 Fairness and regulation: adding DP noise alone does not prevent representation bias; oversmoothing can hide minority patterns and violate fairness statutes (e.g., EU AI Act).
4 Communication-energy trade-off: on edge devices the energy used for model aggregation can dwarf local inference savings; no current anti-oversmoothing pipeline is communication-aware.
5 Security: topology-poisoning attacks mounted by a malicious client can flood the global model with extreme negative-curvature motifs, breaking the Lipschitz guarantees of μC3PO.
idea.methods:
We upgrade μC3PO into FedC3PO—Federated, Fair and α-Stable Curvature-Controlled Causal-Probabilistic ODE—with six new ingredients.

M1  Sketch-Based Federated HαK-F (Fed-HαK-F)
  • Each client keeps a local multi-scale α-stable Koopman filter; only 𝑂(Kr) CMS sketches of the Koopman spectra are sent to the server, ensuring bandwidth ∝ log|E|.
  • Secure aggregation plus count-sketching yields (ϵ_c,δ_c)-DP at the communication level.

M2  Curvature Contrastive Alignment (CoCA)
  • A self-supervised objective aligns the Wasserstein distance between client curvature distributions; prevents the global model from collapsing to the majority curvature mode.
  • Implemented via InfoNCE on the α-stable parameter vectors.

M3  Fair-DP Curvature Perturbation (FDP-Curv)
  • Adds conditional α-stable noise whose scale is inversely proportional to group-specific risk, yielding an analytic bound on Equalised Odds gap ≤ γ.
  • Proved to preserve the global Lipschitz <1 after aggregation.

M4  Communication-Aware Graph Scheduler (Comm-SMiGS)
  • Extends SMiGS with a dual controller that decides when to send updates; objective: minimise (energy + data-transfer) while keeping curvature-forecast variance below θ.
  • Theoretically shown to give an 𝑂(√T) regret bound against an oracle with perfect future power-cap knowledge.

M5  Byzantine-Resilient Flow Defence (BR-Flow)
  • Applies spectral clipping and geometric median aggregation in the latent curvature space; guarantees that up to f malicious clients cannot increase the effective-rank loss by more than Δ.

M6  Shapley-Curv Explainer
  • Computes per-edge Shapley values of the negative log-likelihood in Fed-HαK-F; provides human-readable justifications of which motifs were amplified or damped during training.
idea.experimental_setup:
Datasets / Federated Partitions
• PowerCOVID-Fed: 12 national grids (20 M–35 M edges each) with local power traces.
• Crypto-Tx-Fed: 15 crypto-exchanges, 2-year Ethereum sub-graphs (200 M–450 M edges).
• MIMIC-III-Fed: 10 hospitals, patient-contact graphs (HIPAA compliant).
• ogbn-arxiv, Chameleon, Squirrel (single-client ablation).

Protocols
1 Clients C∈{5,10,20}; rounds R=100; local steps E=5.
2 Privacy budgets: (ϵ_DP,δ) = {(∞,0),(4,10⁻⁵),(1,10⁻⁶)}; communication privacy ϵ_c matched.
3 Adversaries: up to f=⌊0.2C⌋ Byzantine clients insert negative-curvature chains.
4 Fairness: sensitive attribute = region (grid), gender (hospital); evaluate ΔEqualised Odds.
5 Baselines: central μC3PO, FedAvg-GCNII, FedDPS-GCN, FedSAGE-BN, RobustFedCurv (no α-stable).
6 Metrics: Accuracy/mAP, Tail-ECE, ΔEO, RWSI, Comm-Joules, Total Joules, Bits transferred, ϵ_DP & ϵ_c, rank-loss gap, Byzantine-attack degradation.
7 Ablations: disable CoCA, replace FDP-Curv with Laplace, no BR-Flow, no Comm-SMiGS.
idea.expected_result:
• FedC3PO matches central μC3PO accuracy ±0.5 % with only 1.6 × communication overhead at C=20.
• Tail-ECE ≤1.7 %, ΔEqualised Odds ≤1.8 % (vs 7 % for FedAvg-GCNII).
• Comm-SMiGS cuts total (compute + transfer) energy by 35 % over FedAvg; achieves AuPC ≥0.995 across all power-cap traces.
• Under f=20 % Byzantine attack, BR-Flow limits accuracy drop to <2 % while baselines lose >10 %.
• Curvature NLL improves by 45 % over FedDPS-GCN; Shapley-Curv highlights >90 % of high-risk bottleneck edges identified by domain experts.
• Non-asymptotic bound continues to over-estimate empirical rank-loss by <5 % after federated aggregation.
idea.expected_conclusion: FedC3PO demonstrates that heavy-tailed, multi-scale curvature control can be extended to the federated setting while guaranteeing differential privacy, fairness, energy efficiency and robustness to malicious clients.  The proposed sketch-based aggregation and contrastive alignment keep communication low without sacrificing calibration, and the Shapley-Curv explainer bridges the interpretability gap of continuous-depth GNNs.  These results make curvature-aware anti-oversmoothing practical for real-world, cross-organisation deployments in healthcare, energy and finance and establish new benchmarks and metrics for trustworthy federated graph learning.

evaluate.novelty_reason:
Most prior anti-oversmoothing approaches (PairNorm, DGN, ContraNorm, NDLS, PSNR, curvature-rewiring such as BORF) assume a single, centrally stored graph.  None of the cited works addresses (1) a federated scenario where raw edges are siloed, (2) heterogeneous curvature spectra across clients, or (3) simultaneous requirements of differential privacy, fairness, energy-aware communication and Byzantine security.  FedC3PO introduces several mechanisms that are absent from the literature:
• Sketch-based α-stable Koopman spectral summaries (Fed-HαK-F) that allow curvature-controlled message passing to be learned without sharing the graph itself, reducing bandwidth to O(log|E|).
• Curvature Contrastive Alignment (CoCA) that aligns client-level curvature distributions via a self-supervised InfoNCE objective – an idea not explored in existing curvature or normalization methods.
• Fair-DP curvature perturbation with closed-form Equalised-Odds bound, linking anti-oversmoothing and fairness; existing DP-GNNs add Laplace/Gaussian noise but ignore representation bias created by oversmoothing.
• A dual-objective scheduler (Comm-SMiGS) that couples curvature-forecast variance with on-device power caps; previous work on oversmoothing or federated GNNs is communication-agnostic.
• Byzantine-resilient aggregation in latent curvature space (BR-Flow) to mitigate adversarial negative-curvature injections, a threat model absent in earlier analyses.
• Shapley-Curv provides the first path-level explanation for continuous-depth curvature-controlled GNNs.
Together these components move curvature-aware anti-oversmoothing from a theoretical, single-graph setting to a practical, federated, trustworthy pipeline – a gap not covered by the related works list.

Academically, FedC3PO pushes the study of oversmoothing into an unexplored regime – multi-client non-stationary graphs – and couples geometric learning with privacy, fairness and security guarantees.  It also unifies heavy-tailed curvature control with ODE-based continuous-depth models and provides non-asymptotic stability bounds after federated aggregation, likely to stimulate further theoretical work.
Societally, the method targets high-impact domains (healthcare, energy, crypto-finance) where raw graph data cannot be shared.  By reducing communication energy by 35 %, bounding DP leakage, limiting fairness gaps and resisting 20 % Byzantine clients, the approach addresses real regulatory and sustainability constraints.  The Shapley-Curv explainer improves transparency needed for compliance with the EU AI Act.
If empirical claims hold, FedC3PO would make curvature-aware GNNs deployable in real-world silos, thus its potential impact is considerable.
